question: Who has been appointed to head the newly constituted “Judicial Infrastructure Advisory Committee”?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice Aravind Kumar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• Chief Justice of India **Surya Kant** has announced the formation of a high-powered committee to prepare a nationwide roadmap for the modernisation of courts.
 
• The newly constituted “**Judicial Infrastructure Advisory Committee**” will be headed by Supreme Court judge **Justice Aravind Kumar**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The newly constituted “**Judicial Infrastructure Advisory Committee**” will be headed by Supreme Court judge **Justice Aravind Kumar**.
 
• The committee will focus on addressing long-standing infrastructural gaps in the judicial system across the country through enhanced funding and technological upgrades.
 
• The committee will include Justices **Debangsu Basak**, **Ashwani Kumar Mishra** and **Somasekhar Sundaresan** from the Calcutta, Punjab and Haryana, and Bombay high courts respectively.
 
• The director general of the **Central Public Works Department** and the secretary general of the **Supreme Court** will also be part of the panel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The committee will work on seven major areas aimed at improving judicial infrastructure and efficiency, including identifying systemic bottlenecks and enhancing facilities for litigants and lawyers.
 
• The panel will prioritise strengthening the “**e-courts**” initiative to bridge the digital divide in the justice delivery system.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **CJI Surya Kant** seeks a massive financial allocation of **Rs 40,000 crore to Rs 50,000 crore** from the government for judicial infrastructure.
 
• The move is expected to give a major push to judicial reforms and improve access to justice across **India**.
